extracted.intended_audience: romance authors, editors, and writers submitting to RWA/industry contests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for producing a novel-length romance: core genre requirements, subgenre conventions, and commonly-evaluated quality criteria used by RWA and the romance industry (including awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: A central love story
rubrics_metrics.description: "the main plot centers around individuals falling in love and struggling to make the relationship work."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of RWA's two required criteria: the romantic relationship must be the primary plot driver rather than a subplot or background element.

rubrics_metrics.name: An emotionally satisfying and optimistic ending (HEA/HFN)
rubrics_metrics.description: "lovers who risk and struggle for each other and their relationship are rewarded with emotional justice and unconditional love." Often abbreviated HEA (Happily Ever After) or HFN (Happy For Now).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the second required criterion. The ending must provide emotional satisfaction/optimism for the central couple; a bleak or unresolved finale disqualifies the work as romance by RWA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contemporary romance (sub-genre convention)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally evaluated as a subgenre—stories should observe contemporary social norms, technology, and expectations appropriate to modern settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical romance (sub-genre convention)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally evaluated: accuracy in period detail and customs is expected when writing historical romance; anachronisms or neglect of era-specific social dynamics weaken the entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paranormal romance (sub-genre convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative element combined with a central romance arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally evaluated: the speculative/paranormal elements must coexist with and support the romance rather than overshadow or derail the relationship focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Romantic suspense (sub-genre convention)
rubrics_metrics.description: A thriller or suspense plot interwoven with the romance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally evaluated: suspense elements should be integrated so the danger or mystery meaningfully affects the couple and their relationship development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspirational/Christian romance (sub-genre convention)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally evaluated: faith elements should be authentic to the characters and contribute to the romantic arc; sexual content and thematic focus should align with category expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBTQ+ romance (sub-genre convention)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informally evaluated: works with LGBTQ+ leads are evaluated under the same primary criteria (central love story and optimistic ending) while honoring queer-specific experiences and representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Believable chemistry between leads
rubrics_metrics.description: Leads must demonstrate convincing attraction and connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chemistry should arise from characterization, interactions, dialogue, and shared stakes — not just physical descriptions or contrived circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict that organically threatens the relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict should genuinely endanger the couple rather than relying on contrived misunderstandings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using manufactured misunderstandings as lazy plot devices; conflicts should flow logically from characters' motives, circumstances, or external pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Both characters change/grow through the relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Each protagonist should demonstrate development as a result of the relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Growth can be emotional, practical, or moral, but should be believable and tied to the dynamics between the leads rather than arbitrary character rewrites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader should feel the satisfaction of the romantic resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure scenes and beats build toward an emotionally resonant conclusion; pacing and scene selection should maximize reader investment in the couple's outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing of the romance arc
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes expected beats: meet-cute, attraction, obstacle, dark moment, declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The romance arc should progress with clear beats appropriate to the length and subgenre; timing of the 'dark moment' and ultimate reconciliation/commitment is critical for reader satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre conventions respected (HEA/HFN expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers expect HEA/HFN; subverting this expectation disqualifies the work as romance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While innovation within the genre is possible, the fundamental convention of an optimistic romantic resolution must be honored for classification and award consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heat level appropriate to category
rubrics_metrics.description: Sexual/content 'heat' should match the subcategory (ranging from sweet to erotic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All heat levels are valid within their respective categories, but writers should label and position the work to meet reader and category expectations (e.g., category romance vs. erotic romance).
